Thank you for volunteering with Kids PlaySafer Ltd (“Kids PlaySafer”).

1. VOLUNTEER ROLE
Your role as volunteer starts on the date stated hereof. We hope that you will be able to volunteer with us for
at least twelve [12] months so that we can each get the most from the volunteering experience. However,
we are flexible about when you work, within the constraints of drawing up a rota, so please let us know if you
would prefer a different arrangement.
We expect you to perform your role to the best of your ability and to follow our procedures and
standards, including health and safety and equal opportunities, and to comply with our data protection.
policy (where applicable).

2. INDUCTION AND TRAINING
We will provide an induction explaining what we do and how volunteers fit within our organisation. We will also
provide training to assist you to meet the standards we expect from volunteers and to ensure your health and
safety.
3. SUPERVISION AND SUPPORT
Your main point of contact during your volunteering with us is stated above. You will have regular meetings
with your Supervisor to agree targets for your volunteering role and discuss any problems or complaints you
may have. You understand that your placement into volunteer positions is at the sole discretion of Kids
PlaySafer.
Please give your Supervisor as much notice as possible if you are unable to volunteer when expected. You
also understand that the Volunteer's assignment and/or service may be withdrawn or terminated at any time.
4. EXPENSES
Other than any pre-approved expenses by your Supervisor, you will offer your services with no expectation of
pay, benefits, or other privileges of employment of any kind. You acknowledge that, as a volunteer, you will
not be considered an employee of Kids PlaySafer.
5. PERSONAL DATA AND OTHERS
In this paragraph, the following terms are defined as follows:
"Personal Data" means any information about the Volunteer, including but not limited to the Volunteer's name,
address, references, work skills, benefits, management and organizational appraisals and data held for legal
purposes, and shall include information about any next of kin, if appropriate, and/or other persons about whom
data may be collected.
"Processing" or "Process" means carrying out any operation or set of operations on Personal Data
including, but not limited to, collecting, obtaining, organizing, consulting, using, disclosing, or destroying.
5.1 You acknowledge that Kids PlaySafer, by itself or through its contracted service provider, will Process
Personal Data and that this Personal Data may only be used for personnel, administration and management
purposes in connection with this Letter.
5.2 You further understands and agrees that Personal Data may if necessary be transferred to third parties,
including advisors and third parties providing products and services, such as IT systems suppliers and payroll
administrators, as well as regulatory authorities as required by Singapore law.
5.3 By signing this Letter, you expressly consent to the Processing and transfer of Personal Data during and
after the term of this Letter subject to the laws of Singapore.

### Why does voltage drop in series but not parallel?

#### Series

```text
9V ---- Bulb A ---- Bulb B ---- 0V
```

There are **three important points**:

* Before Bulb A = 9 V
* Between bulbs = maybe 4 V
* After Bulb B = 0 V

Bulb A has a voltage drop:

> 9 → 4 V

Bulb B has a voltage drop:

> 4 → 0 V

The drops add up to 9 V.

---

#### Parallel

```text
      9V
       |
   +---+---+
   |       |
 Bulb A  Bulb B
   |       |
   +---+---+
       |
      0V
```

Both bulbs start at **9 V** and end at **0 V**.

So each one gets the full 9 V.

---

## But doesn't the first bulb "use up" the voltage?

This is the key misconception.

The current **splits** *before* it reaches either bulb.

Instead of one stream going through Bulb A and then Bulb B, the charge reaches a junction:

```text
        ↓
       / \
      /   \
 Bulb A  Bulb B
      \   /
       \ /
```

Some charge goes through Bulb A.

Some charge goes through Bulb B.

Neither branch is "after" the other—they are **side by side**.

---

## Think of a mountain

Imagine a mountain that's 9 m high.

Two slides start from the top and end at the ground.

```text
     Top (9 m)

     /      \
Slide A   Slide B

     \      /

   Ground (0 m)
```

Both slides start at the same height and end at the same height.

A person going down **either** slide loses 9 m of gravitational potential energy.

The first slide doesn't make the mountain shorter for the second slide!

A battery works in a similar way:

* The positive terminal is the "top of the mountain."
* The negative terminal is the "bottom."
* Every parallel branch starts at the same "height" (potential) and ends at the same "height."

So every branch gets the same voltage.

---

One tiny thing to fix from your earlier thinking: **voltage is not a quantity that gets used up.** What gets transferred is **energy**. Voltage measures **how much energy each coulomb of charge loses** between two points. In a parallel circuit, each coulomb in each branch still falls through the same energy difference because every branch connects the same two battery terminals.

You're getting very close to a deep understanding. The next natural question is usually:

> **If every branch gets the full voltage, where does the extra current come from?**

The answer to that ties together voltage, current, and why adding more parallel branches makes the battery supply more total current.
